text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Costas Simitis and Pasok win the Greek elections.
- Nearly 16 million pounds in redundancy pay will be given to employees in 1996.
- President Glafcos Clerides sees the possibility of talks starting in Cyprus in 1997.
- Pasok wins the Greek elections. The Greek Communist Party KKE comes third.
- American ambassadors in Greece, Cyprus and Turkey met in Athens to discuss the latest developments concerning the Cyprus problem.
- Simitis is to turn his attention to national issues and the economy.
- The Greek Prime Minister is expected to visit Cyprus.
- Technocrats will be running the island's hospitals.
- Costas Simitis is confronted with problems and dilemmas after yesterday's victory in the Greek elections.
- New Democracy party leader Miltiadis Evert resigns.
- Without common ground we will not be going to talks, says President Clerides.
- Woman is suspected of stabbing her husband in front of their small child.
